newsitem.title: UK: US Gulf interest seen crucial to Ldn freight rates.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf interest seen crucial to Ldn freight rates.

text.p: Appreciating rates for Panamaxes in the Pacific were the main reason for an increase of 6 points in the BFI to 1,069.

But brokers regard the US Gulf as the crucial area this week to point the way of the freight market in the immediate future. The evidence so far available on Monday suggests that modern Panamaxes will continue to enjoy firm conditions but the older types may fall further behind.

Caper rates have remained pretty static although a growing reluctance by owners to trade to the Far East has become apparent. This is explained by the anticipated delivery of a number of newbuildings from Eastern yards which are being delayed until January 1977 and which are expected to affect rates adversely.

Brokers believe Handy rates are set to rise in the US Gulf but the Continent is flat and S America continues weak. The Far East is reported to be a little more active for Handies although sugar rates have eased from australia.

Vesta Island is reported fixed by NYK for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for early Nov at $21.00 basis no combo - 50 cents up on Hanjin's fixture of Full Comfort last week for Nov 13/23 and $1.00 on MOSK's fixture of C. Yalikoy for early Nov reported in the middle of last week. On the other hand the 1974-built Aurelia 61,448 dwt has been fixed at a poor level delivery prompt US Gulf trip Far East at a shade over $8,000 daily plus under $100,000onus.
Another weak Atlantic fixture was Cargill's 60,000 grains 53' Plate and Brazil/Continent for end Oct at $13.75 basis 2-1.

New Panamax grain enquiry in the Atlantic included Andre delivery US Gulf Oct 20/30 trip Singapore-Japan range, Seatrans 55/60,000 dwt US Gulf Oct/Nov trip Taiwan and Tradigrain 75,000 barley St Lawrence/Jeddah for Oct 30/Nov 5.

In the Handy section Finagrain were said to be struggling to cover a prompt stem of 30,000/30,800 HSS US Gulf/Algeria in excess of $20.00 and Continental fixed Lakes/Turkey on private terms. New business included Continental 25,000/10 HSS US Gulf/Tunisia and Andre 25,000/5 HSS US Gulf/Aqaba Nov 10/20.

A fairly uneventful start to the week saw reports of coal business involving Anangel Ambition 150,264 dwt Roberts Bank/S Korea and Bulk Tirreno 145,000 dwt Banjermasin/Pori but full details were not available. Safore were understood to have booked two consecutive stems of 95,000/10 iron ore Saldanha/Qingdao for early next year with EMS Ore. Interbulk were said to have covered 3 Caper coal stems Richards Bay/Denmark for first half 1997 at $6.25.
Noble are believed to have fixed Andros 64,000 dwt for ironore Goa/China and NYK a Shinwa Panamax with Petcoke long Beach/Japan, both on private terms.

Holly 29,000 dwt was fixed Continent/S E Africa but details have not yet emerged. Fednav have been linked with Ayane 27,080 dwt delivery Continent for a trip via Lakes redelivery Montreal at $9,000 daily, and possibly also with Luna Verde 28,360 dwt for Lakes business.

Brokers report a shortage of Handy tonnage in the US Gulf. In the East Polydefkis P 22,235 dwt open prompt Japan has fixed privately and Anangel Honesty 31,774 dwt has been booked on subjects NoPac/Far East at close to $6,250 daily plus $120,000 BB. The Mark 2 Freedom Anangel Victory 17,188 dwt has also fixed on subjects from Australia or NoPac about $5,100 daily plus $50,000 bonus.
